correctness.rationale: C: Smoothness by gradient and separable double cover; the 16+12 explicit split bitangents exhaust 28 by classical theorem. An exhaustive standalone GF(25) enumeration visits each of 651 base points once, counts 826 rational surface points, 778 over the 28 bitangent lines and 48 outside, identifies exactly the 24 claimed base projections, and verifies their single orbit. All 56 exceptional components lie over the 28 lines. Only this finite-field claim is proved; no unbounded numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: V: The number of points outside all 56 exceptional curves is precisely the natural fullness invariant in Knecht–Reyes; they leave q=25 as a possible field size. The highly symmetric split Fermat candidate has an exact 48-point failure, with a conceptual 24-point axis locus and a single symmetry orbit. This is a motivated arithmetic incidence result at an outstanding small field, beyond recomputing 28 classical bitangents; no classification of other surfaces is claimed.
